items.quote: J'ai rarement trouvé des jeux à la hauteur de leur hype, et je dois dire que Expedition 33 fait exception, c'est une masterclass sur bien des domaines et les "géants du AAA" feraient bien d'en tirer des conclusions. L'univers est intrigant, les personnages sont bien caractérisés et l'on s'y attache, les voix FR sont d'une qualité exceptionnelle et la bande son magistrale. Le système de combat n'invente rien, mais réussit à s'approprier diverses mécaniques d'autres licences au service de combats dynamiques, et de personnages que l'on peut personnaliser selon ses préférences et/ou les ennemis rencontrés. Le scénario enfin, m'a complètement embarqué du début à la fin, merci à chacun des créateurs de cette œuvre magnifique qui fait pour moi partie du panthéon des RPG, et du jeu vidéo en général.

items.quote:
After playing the game I feel its just the hype and nothing else.

Bad Nier copy - They try to create a mystery like Nier and add similar music. But Nier's music feels original and connects you to the world. Expedition 33 music sounds like its an afterthought. It has no connection with area or bosses. Its just like "Lets make it like nier so it sound cool"

Bad Elden Ring copy - The game shows you a paintress just like Elden Ring shows you Erdtree. But Elden Ring keeps the tree in picture no matter where you go and entire world connects with the erdtree, Marika and the past. Clair Obscure feels like world and story was an after thought again. They were like "Lets show something like Elden Ring's Erdtree and then build story around it". The story doesnt feel original.

Bad Final Fantasy copy - The characters seem like Final Fantasy games. But in Final Fantasy no matter which one it is the characters are well connected with each other. Each one with their back stories. Expedition 33 tells nothing about most of the characters. They are like they are just party members with powers and nothing else.Exploration is nonexistent. You have very linear pathways.

Areas in the game feel like they have 0 history. They just look good but why they are like that and why we are there is nowhere told. In all 3 games above we are told some background of the areas and even bosses. Expedition 33 tells nothing about anything. Just make it look like a fantasy land.

Objects in the game are again just copy paste of above games. Lets put a Rose underwater. Lets out random objects at places they dont belong to create a mystery. Why? Why dont create something original than just creating **** copy paste of other games without adding meaning to anything.

Few goods:

Combat is good. Parry, dodge is similar to Persona games but feel slightly better.

Overall look an feel. Game looks good on surface if you dont ask questions why.

Good performance. Game performs good even in steam deck all the way to RTX 4080.

Overall the game won a goty and so many awards make me feel Nier, FF7 and Elden Ring are far original than Expedition 33. This game works but anybody who has played above games will say the same that its a meaningless copy paste. i.e. game copies a lot but forgets to add meaning to it.

By the way the community is toxic as hell. Its true that game steals a lot from other games but if you talk with any community member they outright deny it. Reddit mods will just close your posts if you say anything against the game.

items.quote:
I started playing Clair Obscur a little over a year after its release. I like doing that with major games that receive a huge amount of media coverage.
There are several advantages to it: it protects me from the hype and from potential disappointment if I had built up too many expectations, and by then, all the major bug-fixing patches have often already been released.

Anyway, I started Clair Obscur a little over 15 days ago, in July 2026...Right from the start, the game’s overall technical quality is the first thing that stands out. And yet, we’re still only in the prologue, in Lumière—the rest of the game will keep driving that point home.
The story unfolds gradually, and its plot hooks you fairly quickly because the premise is quite original.
The turn-based combat system, which I first discovered with the original PlayStation version of Final Fantasy VII and have always enjoyed, is enhanced here by an exceptional sense of dynamism.
That said, you won’t grasp all of its possibilities right away. You need to take your time and accept that it may take a few hours to learn the **** at some point, it will click. And when it does, believe me: the rest of the game will be absolutely exhilarating!

I’ll try to keep this brief so I don’t end up writing an entire novel: I completed my first playthrough in a straight line, without doing any side quests, because I wanted answers about the outcome of this captivating story.
And I wasn’t disappointed. It’s simply exceptional.

I haven’t mentioned the music yet: it’s magnificent and perfectly complements the atmosphere.What an incredible achievement! 

Such a small team managing to create a work of this scale… Hats off to you, Sandfall! Bravo, Mr. Broche. A debut production that’s nothing short of a masterclass.
